questions.q: Why was Ben Gunn sure the flag over the stockade belonged to Jim's friends?
choices: Silver would have flown the Jolly Roger instead
He could see the doctor's face looking over the fence
He had heard the squire's voice calling from the trees
The pirates had sworn never to fly any flag on the island
questions.evidence: Silver would fly the Jolly Roger, you don't make no doubt of that

questions.q: According to Ben Gunn, who built the old stockade years ago?
choices: Captain Flint
Silver
Billy Bones
Captain Smollett
questions.evidence: as was made years and years ago by Flint

questions.q: How did Ben Gunn say the person who comes to meet him must come?
choices: Alone, with a white thing in his hand
At midnight, carrying a lit lantern
With Jim beside him and two pistols ready
By boat around the island from the ship
questions.evidence: him that comes is to have a white thing in his hand, and he's to come alone

questions.q: What made Jim and Ben Gunn suddenly run off in different directions?
choices: A cannonball crashed into the sand nearby
Silver and his men stepped out of the trees
A rattling snake struck at them from the grass
They heard the ship's bell
questions.evidence: a cannonball came tearing through the trees and pitched in the sand

questions.q: What flag did Jim see flying from the HISPANIOLA at sunset?
choices: The Jolly Roger, the black flag of piracy
The Union Jack, the red, white and blue
A white flag asking for a truce
No flag at all, only a bare mast
questions.evidence: there was the Jolly Roger--the black flag of piracy--flying from her peak

questions.q: Why did Jim take note of the tall white rock on the sandy spit?
choices: It might be where Ben Gunn kept his boat
It marked the spot where Flint buried his treasure
It was safe from the cannonballs
It was where Silver and the pirates had made camp
questions.evidence: this might be the white rock of which Ben Gunn had spoken

questions.q: What was used as a basin for the spring under the porch of the log-house?
choices: An iron ship's kettle with the bottom knocked out
A wooden rum barrel that had been sawed in half
A stone bowl that Flint's men had carved long ago
An old sea-chest lined with pitch to hold the water
questions.evidence: a great ship's kettle of iron, with the bottom knocked out

questions.q: What two things made life inside the log-house uncomfortable that evening?
choices: Blowing sand and smoke that would not go out the roof
Heavy rain dripping in and swarms of biting mosquitoes
Snakes in the corners and rats running over the floor
Loud singing and shouting from the pirates on the ship
questions.evidence: There was sand in our eyes, sand in our teeth, sand in our suppers

questions.q: How did Captain Smollett keep the tired party from falling into low spirits?
choices: He gave everyone jobs and went around helping them
He let them all rest and sleep until the next morning
He told them long stories about his past voyages at sea
He handed out extra brandy to each man to cheer him up
questions.evidence: If we had been allowed to sit idle, we should all have fallen in the blues

questions.q: What did Dr. Livesey secretly carry in his snuff-box?
choices: A piece of Parmesan cheese
A few gold coins
A copy of the map
Medicine for fever
questions.evidence: in my snuff-box I carry a piece of Parmesan cheese

questions.q: Jim says he is "not very sure whether he's sane" about Ben Gunn. "Sane" means:
choices: Having a healthy, sound mind
Being kind to others
Being strong and healthy in body
Being honest and always truthful
questions.evidence: I am not very sure whether he's sane

questions.q: What were the "two able allies" the leaders counted on to weaken the pirates?
choices: Rum and the unhealthy climate
Ben Gunn and the cannon
Hunger and the cold night air
The tide and the shifting wind
questions.evidence: we had two able allies--rum and the climate

questions.q: What woke Jim the next morning?
choices: Shouts about a flag of truce and Silver himself
A cannonball smashing through the log-house roof
Ben Gunn calling his name from outside the fence
The captain ringing the ship's bell for the watch
questions.evidence: "Flag of truce!" I heard someone say

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: Jim leaves Ben Gunn, rejoins his friends, and settles into the stockade
Jim slips away alone at night and captures the HISPANIOLA by himself
The pirates storm the stockade at dawn and capture the log-house
Ben Gunn leads the doctor through the woods straight to the treasure
questions.evidence: was soon warmly welcomed by the faithful party
